text:
Kaedan Korczak spent his first 155 NHL games in Vegas as a defence-first depth defenceman. In Pittsburgh he's playing 18 minutes a night and producing like a different player: ten points in 18 games, every one of them an assist, including two against his old team on Nov. 3 and two more against Boston two nights later.

Don't expect the pace to hold. Our talent range has his scoring rate well above where it should settle, and he's never been a big point producer. What should hold is the defence. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.6 wins above replacement last season, 41st among defencemen, almost all of it from even-strength defence, with opponents getting noticeably fewer chances when he was out there (97th percentile). The Penguins have taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five this season, better than without him. The weak spot, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: only 29% of his exits keep possession, so watch for pucks off the glass when teams forecheck him hard. He has yet to score; a 92nd-percentile shot says he could.
